title: fix: handle invalid JSON responses in CouchDB handlers
notes: Closed without merging. Its comments (an issue-first request, a template reminder, a stale notice, an unrelated SonarCloud comment) were checked and give no findings away; there was no human code review. The fix itself is sound; the defects are in its tests and in how the 502 is sent.

code-review.notes: `severity` is the severity the finding deserves, taken from OCR's own ratings: the most common across the runs that reported it, the higher one on a tie; a comment that covers several items gives its severity only to the item that is its main point. `extra_credit` holds correct findings a review earns credit for but isn't marked down for missing.

required.summary: The new routing.spec.js tests exercise an inline copy of the proxyForAuth handler, never the real one in api/src/routing.js, so they would still pass if the fix were reverted.
required.match: Says the tests don't load or run the real routing.js handler. Only pointing out that `routing` and `proxyForAuthHandler` are unused is not a match: that is routing-spec-unused-vars.

required.summary: infodoc.spec.js assigns recordDocumentWrite/recordDocumentWrites stubs onto the controller's own exports, but the controller calls the @medic/infodoc library, so the stubs are never invoked and the real library runs. Under `npm run unit-api` (UNIT_TEST_ENV=1) db.sentinel is replaced by a guard that logs and calls process.exit(1), so the file's first success-path test exits the whole mocha run: none of the later tests, in this spec or any other api spec, execute.
required.match: Says the stubs are on the wrong object, so the code under test never calls them. Saying the run then exits or hits the real db is part of the same item. Only saying they should use sinon.stub so sinon.restore() undoes them is not a match: that is infodoc-stubs-not-restored.

required.summary: The 502 is hand-written with res.status(502).json({ error, details }) instead of the serverUtils error helpers used elsewhere in the same handler, so it lacks the `code` field and Accept-based content negotiation of the API's standard error envelope.
required.match: Points at serverUtils (error/serverError/writeJSON) or the API's standard error shape as what the 502 should use.

required.summary: copyProxyHeaders has already copied the upstream status message and headers (including Content-Type) onto res before the parse fails, and res.json() keeps an existing Content-Type, so the JSON 502 goes out labelled as e.g. text/html.
required.match: Says the 502 response carries the upstream's headers or Content-Type.

required.summary: Logging a 100-character preview of the unparseable upstream body could put sensitive data in the logs. The PR states the preview as a feature, but proxyForAuth serves offline users' document reads, and a truncated response (one of the PR's own triggers) can begin with patient data.
required.match: Says the logged body preview could expose sensitive data. A comment only about the log level or format is not a match.

required.summary: The infodoc.spec.js test claiming to record only successful writes from a partial bulk response asserts only that the bulk stub was called, never which ids it got, so forwarding the failed doc too would still pass.
required.match: Says the partial-bulk test doesn't check which ids were recorded, so it can't tell that the failed doc was filtered out. The same point about the other tests is weak-test-assertions.

required.summary: infodoc.spec.js tests assert only that a stub was called, or only the log template, not the ids or message passed (e.g. the chunked-data and bulk-write tests, and 'should log error with status code and error message').
required.match: Says an infodoc.spec.js test other than the partial-bulk one asserts only that something was called, or only part of what was logged, not the arguments it claims to check.

required.summary: `routing` and `proxyForAuthHandler` in routing.spec.js are declared but never assigned or used.
required.match: Says `routing` and/or `proxyForAuthHandler` are declared but never assigned or used, as its own comment or inside a broader one. Saying only that the tests don't run the real handler is not a match: that is routing-tests-copy-handler.

required.summary: The try/catch around JSON.parse is duplicated between routing.js and infodoc.js; extract a shared helper.
required.match: Says the parse-and-catch logic is duplicated across routing.js and infodoc.js, or suggests a shared helper for it.

extra_credit.summary: infodoc.spec.js replaces recordDocumentWrite/recordDocumentWrites by plain assignment rather than sinon.stub, so afterEach's sinon.restore() never undoes it. True, but harmless: the property lands on the controller's exports, which nothing reads, and no other spec loads that controller. It goes away once infodoc-stubs-miss is fixed.
extra_credit.match: Says the assignments are never restored by sinon.restore(). Saying it overwrites @medic/infodoc is a match too, though wrong in detail: the assignments land on the controller's exports.

extra_credit.summary: When the body can't be parsed, infodoc skips the metadata update even if the write succeeded, leaving infodocs stale; log at a higher level. The PR states this choice and why: the doc ids can't be recovered from an unparseable body.
extra_credit.match: Says a successful write can go unrecorded in the infodocs when its response can't be parsed.

extra_credit.summary: A body of `null` is valid JSON, so it skips the catch, and `body.id` then throws a TypeError in infodoc.js, the same class of crash the PR is fixing.
extra_credit.match: Says a body that parses to null (or another non-object) gets past the catch and throws on `body.id`.

extra_credit.summary: The early return on parse failure skips audit.expressCallback, so the request leaves no audit entry.
extra_credit.match: Says the early return on a parse failure skips audit.expressCallback, so the request isn't audited.

extra_credit.summary: The handler always responds 502, discarding a meaningful upstream status (e.g. 403/404) that came with a non-JSON body.
extra_credit.match: Says the upstream status code is replaced by 502 and should be passed through when meaningful. Comments about the 502's body or headers are 502-bypasses-serverutils or 502-inherits-upstream-headers.

requirements.notes: Reports split and merge requirements differently from run to run, so each item is matched by meaning, and one report item may cover several. `status` is the bucket it should land in; `acceptable` lists other buckets that are not counted as a miss. Report items for trivial PR bullets (the logger import, the parsedBody rename, the test count) match nothing and are not scored. `preconditions_to_confirm` holds the operational facts the skill should list under 'Preconditions to confirm'; empty means it should say None. `rejected` holds findings reviews have made that are wrong.

required.summary: infodoc.js catches the JSON.parse failure, logs a warning with the upstream status code and error message, and returns early without recording an infodoc write.
required.match: A Delivered item saying infodoc.js catches the parse failure, logs it and skips the infodoc write. Separate items for the catch, the log and the early return together match.

required.summary: routing.js catches the JSON.parse failure in the proxyForAuth handler and logs an error with the status code, error message and a 100-character body preview.
required.match: A Delivered item saying routing.js catches the parse failure and logs it with the status, error and body preview.

required.summary: routing.js responds 502 with error details on a parse failure, returning early so no second response is sent, so the request completes. Before the fix it didn't hang, as the PR and issue say: the throw reached api/server.js's uncaughtException handler, which logs and exits the API process.
required.match: A Delivered item for the 502 response or for the request completing instead of hanging. Pending verification matches only when it names the upstream headers / Content-Type copied onto res (see code-review 502-inherits-upstream-headers). A report saying the old behaviour was a crash rather than a hang matches too.

required.summary: Valid JSON responses keep their existing behaviour, including interceptResponse and the audit callback in routing.js and the infodoc recording.
required.match: A Delivered item saying valid JSON responses follow the existing path unchanged.

required.summary: infodoc.spec.js error-path tests (HTML page, truncated JSON, empty body, non-UTF8 bytes, logging) call the real handler and are correct in themselves. But under `npm run unit-api` they never run: the file's first success-path test exits the mocha process (see code-review infodoc-stubs-miss).
required.match: A Delivered item for the error-path tests, or one that cites them as tests of the error handling. Not delivered matches only when the reason is that the earlier success-path tests exit or block the run.

required.summary: The promised success-path regression tests (valid JSON, chunked data, bulk writes) don't test anything: their stubs are assigned onto the controller's exports, while the controller calls @medic/infodoc. Under `npm run unit-api` the first of them also exits the mocha run (api/src/db.js:65).
required.match: Not delivered because the stubs are never invoked. Delivered, or Not delivered for some other reason, is a miss.

required.summary: The promised routing.js tests (502 generation, error logging, chunked invalid bodies, valid-JSON regression) run an inline copy of the handler and never load api/src/routing.js.
required.match: Not delivered because the tests don't exercise the real handler. Delivered, or Not delivered for some other reason, is a miss.

required.summary: The issue's 'at least these locations' is covered: these are the only JSON.parse(body.toString()) call sites under api/src.
required.match: A Delivered item saying no other unguarded JSON.parse of a CouchDB response remains in the API.

rejected.summary: Precondition to confirm: @medic/logger must be resolvable from api/src/controllers/infodoc.js at runtime.
rejected.reason: The API already uses @medic/logger throughout; it is not an operational fact this change depends on.
rejected.match: Lists @medic/logger (or the logger import) being available or resolvable as a precondition.

undisclosed_changes.notes: Every changed file (two sources, two specs) is described in the PR, so the expected answer is None. `rejected` holds findings reviews have made that are wrong.

rejected.summary: Undisclosed change: routing.spec.js declares `routing` and `proxyForAuthHandler`, never assigned or read, next to an empty before() hook.
rejected.reason: Part of the routing tests the PR describes, so not an undisclosed change. The real problem is the routing-tests requirement.
rejected.match: Lists the unused `routing` / `proxyForAuthHandler` declarations, or the empty before() hook, as an undisclosed change.

required.summary: Use the serverUtils error helpers (error/serverError, backed by writeJSON), already used in the same handler, instead of the hand-written res.status(502).json(...): they give the standard { code, error, details } envelope, Accept-based content negotiation and a headersSent guard.
required.match: Cites serverUtils as the existing way to send the error. Mentioning the missing `code` field or a needed 502 branch alongside it is part of the same item.

required.summary: routing.spec.js already uses rewire, which would let the new tests reach and run the real proxyRes handler instead of a copy.
required.match: Cites rewire (or the existing rewire usage) as a way to test the real handler.
